heuristic.applicability: Prefer when the held peg and TCP enter displaced together from the retrieval skill, the two-frame peg-to-TCP transform is stable, and the observed hole remains within reachable transport range. This policy is intended for source/held-object displacement and modest orientation variation under a valid grasp, especially during lift and high-clearance reorientation.

handoff.entry_conditions: Require closed fingers and a peg/TCP relative transform that is approximately stable over the two causal frames; use after retrieval has coupled the peg to the TCP. Entry may be at the nominal low lift or later in incoming overlap, but stable observed geometry is only a proxy for grasp, not contact truth.
handoff.exit_conditions: Continue through reorientation and transport; hand off once peg-to-hole geometry indicates near axis alignment and lateral centering above the hole, or later during the demonstrated descent/early-insertion overlap.
handoff.failure_signatures: Peg motion is not coupled to TCP motion, peg-to-TCP offset drifts, fingers open, source displacement creates an unreachable route, box/lid clearance is lost, or hole-relative error does not shrink. No demonstrated labels support reacquisition after a drop or collision recovery.
handoff.overlap_role: The full [1120,1500) labels are retained, including [1120,1270) with retrieval and [1380,1500) with alignment/insertion. The peg anchor is re-resolved at each replan, preserving action-supervised overlap rather than trimming it.
handoff.successor_readiness: Prefer align_and_insert_peg when the peg is stably held, approximately identity-oriented, and centered above the hole with descent underway. If the destination itself is displaced substantially, the hole-frame prior is the stronger continuation.

heuristic.limitations: The construction assumes the observed peg pose is a meaningful, stably held anchor. It cannot infer contact truth and is unsafe as a dropped-peg recovery policy. If the peg alone moves while the hole is fixed, the required endpoint changes in peg coordinates and must still be inferred from the observed hole-to-peg relation; large changes remain out of support. Peg-frame rotation also changes obstacle geometry. Use the hole-frame prior for destination displacement and the current-TCP local prior when peg pose is unreliable but the TCP state is trustworthy.
heuristic.pipeline_implications: Select using two-frame peg/TCP coupling, not gripper closure alone. Refresh the peg anchor every 8-step replan, preserve causal history over switches, keep gripper closure learned from the demonstrations, and reject/interrupt on obvious anchor drift or failed IK diagnostics. Use the incoming overlap for robust takeover from retrieval and the outgoing overlap for transfer to insertion.
heuristic.rationale: At index 1120 the observed peg centers vary from about x -0.610 to -0.622 and z 0.028-0.040, with matching TCP variation; all inspected commands keep gripper -1. The demonstrations then lift above the 0.05 m wall and turn while the peg remains offset from the TCP, reaching high-clearance z about 0.43-0.48 around 1240-1270 before transport. Deployment may deliver a similarly grasped peg at a shifted source or intermediate pose. Representing the complete 16-slot commanded TCP sequence in the newest observed peg frame makes the learned lift/reorientation/transport targets transform with a rigid displacement of the held peg by construction. Conditioning on two-frame peg-to-TCP geometry, hole-in-peg geometry, qpos, and qvel retains grasp configuration, destination, and reachability dependence. The expected benefit applies only to stable-grasp displacements and is not demonstrated recovery.
heuristic.statement: Held-peg anchor prior: diffuse future commanded TCP poses as position plus 6D rotation relative to the currently observed peg pose, with two-frame attachment geometry and robot state as condition. Compose predictions with the replan-time peg pose before shared IK, giving rigid source/held-object displacement equivariance under a stable grasp.

assignment.subgoal: Maintain the peg grasp while lifting to clearance, turning the peg into the square-hole axis, transporting it above the target, and staging it through descent and the first part of insertion.

check.checkpoint_selection: last EMA at the declared update budget

conversion_check.description: For demonstration labels, decoded IK FK must reproduce the commanded TCP in position/rotation and preserve the gripper scalar within maximum error 0.005. Rotation projection is exact for encoded rotations; joint nonuniqueness is allowed and all IK diagnostics are exposed.

contract.cut_relation: All twelve assigned [1120,1500) action ranges are retained. This includes incoming retrieval overlap [1120,1270) and outgoing insertion overlap [1380,1500). Only the Cartesian label frame changes to the causal peg anchor.
contract.output_semantics: Each slot is an unnormalized Cartesian TCP target [p_peg(3 metres), R_peg_tcp first-two rotation-matrix columns(6), gripper(1)] relative to the newest causal peg_pose fixed for the sampled chunk. Slots denote t-1 through t+14; slots 1-8 execute. Decoding projects 6D orientation to SO(3), composes T_world_peg*T_peg_tcp, and calls panda_kinematics.solve_ik from freshly measured qpos. A deterministic orthogonal fallback handles only degenerate sampled 6D vectors. The native gripper scalar is passed through unchanged.
contract.parameter_semantics: No high-level numeric parameters. The caller passes an empty object. At each replan, the adapter resolves the newest observed peg_pose as the SE(3) action reference; this call is appropriate only after high-level selection judges the peg to be stably held.
